header_summary:
A new draft standard for proving Bitcoin transaction inclusion using wtxid consolidates prior approaches from Knots, Electrum, and Core, and introduces explicit validation rules, extensive test vectors, and two distinct proof formats. To address edge cases, such as block 481823, and to ensure secure verification across full and lightweight clients, the proposal recommends rejecting certain Merkle proofs and introduces “segwit is active for this block” as a mandatory input; the draft is available for review at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/witness-inclusion-proofs/bip-witness-inclusion-proofs.md) and further discussion is encouraged ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/C899B11E-4971-4AAF-8BA3-81EBAFBF7739@jeanpablo.jp/T/#u#meb2b2f0670b30c170d2e4099b87537be5c558448)).

Concerns over quantum threats to Bitcoin have led to proposals like landmine soft forks and auctions, enabling owners of legacy coins to reclaim or protect their assets if quantum attacks occur. These frameworks balance transparency, fairness, and practicality by using collateralization, commit/reveal mechanisms, and incentivized auctions to deter attackers and prioritize rightful owners ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/ffd99327-f633-4e2e-bc54-cc1389ffebccn@googlegroups.com/T/#m42c65c2f95715f2c259265b3f98c68dea5dcdcd2)).

Recent security advisories have prompted the release of fixed versions [31.3](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-31.3/) and [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-30.5/); users of version 29.x are urged to upgrade, while version 32.1 already includes the necessary fixes ([advisory details](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/), [mailing list thread](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/c47ceea6-99de-41fe-a97c-928881963eccn@googlegroups.com/T/u)).

Technical discussions have also addressed transaction propagation analysis, storage optimization using RocksDB and LZ4 compression in [exnode](https://github.com/brunoerg/exnode), and the integration of BIP-361 with PACTs to enable anonymous, quantum-resistant asset protection while preserving long-term ownership rights ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-bitcoin-quantum-roadmap-combining-bip-361-and-pacts-to-preserve-ownership-rights/3122)).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Witness Transaction Inclusion Proofs
recent_posts.summary: - A draft consolidates previous approaches to standardize transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid.  - It defines two proof formats, details validation steps, and provides extensive test vectors.  - Feedback is requested to improve interoperability and finalize decisions on required formats and byte padding.

recent_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
recent_posts.summary: - The landmine soft fork allows owners of vulnerable legacy coins to reclaim assets after quantum attacks.  - Auctions and collateralization are proposed to deter attackers and enable fair recovery of compromised coins.  - Transparent tracking of quantum-safe coins is crucial for effective migration and protocol governance.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: - Two new software releases address a medium severity security vulnerability in major supported versions.  - Users with version 29.x are strongly urged to upgrade for improved security and reliability.  - Detailed vulnerability information and policy guidance are available through official advisories and the mailing list.

recent_posts.title: Exploiting Wallet Rebroadcast to Link Addresses to Node IPs and More
recent_posts.summary: - Previously broadcasted transactions are ignored by nodes, making tracking attempts using them unreliable.  - Identifying a transaction's source is difficult because intermediary nodes may relay transactions multiple times.  - Generating new transactions for the target and using Replace-By-Fee improves tracking accuracy and reduces costs.

recent_posts.title: Reducing Bitcoin Full Node Storage Without Consensus Changes
recent_posts.summary: - RocksDB organizes data into 4 KiB blocks, enabling efficient lookups and enhancing system performance.  - LZ4 compression reduces index block size with minimal CPU overhead, excluding large blob values.  - Compression lowers disk usage but raises CPU and memory needs, occasionally increasing latency with heavier codecs.

recent_posts.title: A Bitcoin Quantum Roadmap: Combining BIP-361 and PACTs to Preserve Ownership Rights
recent_posts.summary: - The roadmap introduces quantum-resistant addresses, anonymous PACTs, and a migration period freezing vulnerable mechanisms.  - A quantum canary halts new registrations at security thresholds, while matured PACTs enable indefinite fund recovery.  - The approach enables anonymous asset security, minimizes theft risk, and balances community interests.

active_posts.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts.summary: - Substantial progress was made in BIP management, improving submissions, discussions, and repository vitality.  - Key advancements involved process updates, resolving abandoned submissions, and enhancing integration scripts.  - A refreshed editor team of three active members is proposed to ensure sustainable and collaborative progress.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal introduces an optional P2P messaging system for sharing stale tip information.  - Nodes communicate about recently observed stale tips, supporting better diagnostics and quicker network reorganization.  - Technical limits ensure relevant data transmission, with each node caching up to ten recent stale tips.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
active_posts.summary: - SHRINCS is a new hash-based signature scheme offering compactness, post-quantum security, and fast verification.  - The draft is a prototype needing peer review, security proofs, and robust state management in software.  - Community feedback and discussion are encouraged to refine SHRINCS, improve clarity, and ensure security.

active_posts.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
active_posts.summary: - New timewarp attack rules restrict block timestamps to prevent blockchain manipulation and maintain integrity.  - A mathematical formula ensures the blockchain's length is bounded, even under various manipulation scenarios.  - Formal proofs confirm these rules effectively secure blockchain growth, offering reliable protection against attacks.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: 324-byte stateful post-quantum signatures with static backups
active_posts.summary: - SHRINCS merges stateful and stateless signature schemes for both efficiency and robust fallback security.  - Its unbalanced XMSS tree and WOTS+C scheme optimize signature size and signing performance for few uses.  - Dual-mode operation allows secure fallback to stateless signatures if state integrity is lost or uncertain.

active_posts.title: State minimization in MuSig2 signing sessions
active_posts.summary: - The proposed method enables devices with limited storage to efficiently manage multi-input transaction signing.  - Synthetic randomness is derived for each input and key pair using a global random number and hashing.  - The approach ensures security, supports session management, and references collaborative work and relevant technical links.

today_in_history_posts.title: Formal specification of Miniscript in Alloy
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A formal specification of Miniscript in Alloy analyzer is now available on Github.  - This specification supports implementation, test generation, validation, extension, and properties exploration of Miniscript.  - Reviewers are encouraged to share feedback and report any inconsistencies they discover on Github.

today_in_history_posts.title: SIGHASH_SINGLE + update_fee Considered Harmful
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A vulnerability in Lightning Network allows attackers to bypass penalties by exploiting HTLC fee malleability.  - Tighter channel policies and adopting justice transactions with higher fees are recommended countermeasures.  - Updating fee assignment methods and limiting unreasonable fee rates could mitigate the identified risks.

today_in_history_posts.title: Thoughts on scaling and consensus changes (2023)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Scaling Bitcoin for billions requires around 50,000 off-chain entities like federated sidechains and Chaumian ecash banks.  - Efficient security, regulatory compliance, and auditability are essential for these entities, including quick Layer 1 exits.  - Ongoing development prioritizes correlated failure prevention, second-layer tools, and innovations like coinpools and Utreexo.
